# #720 — validate-pr-body falls back to the validator's OWN tree, so a Done-means check absent from the branch under review passes on the primary checkout's copy

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-10T14:18:54Z
Updated: 2026-08-10T14:38:53Z
Closed: 2026-08-10T14:38:53Z

## Family classification

**Family A** — a gate judging from the WRONG TREE. Direct residue of #706/#709,
in the same file those lanes repaired.

## Defect

`scripts/validate-pr-body.ts:91` derives a second search tree from the
validator's own location:

```ts
const OWN_TREE = resolve(import.meta.dir, "..");
```

`requireDoneMeans` searches the tree under review FIRST (correct, #706), then
**falls back to `OWN_TREE`** (lines 157-158). Because the hook runs the PRIMARY
checkout's copy of the validator (`REPO_ROOT` is `import.meta.url`-derived,
line 95), `OWN_TREE` is always the primary checkout.

So a `Done-means:` path that does **not exist in the branch under review**
PASSES whenever a file of that name happens to exist in the primary checkout.
The verdict is decided by a tree that is not the one being merged — the precise
defect #706 was filed for, surviving as the fallback rather than the primary
lookup.

## Reproduction

```
$ mkdir -p $TMPW/gate-audit/faketree     # a review tree with no done-means dir

$ PR_BODY='## Summary
Audit reproduction.

## Verification
- Done-means: scripts/done-means/705-pre-push-base-selection.sh
- [x] Tests pass' \
  PR_TITLE=repro PR_REPO_DIR=$TMPW/gate-audit/faketree \
  bun scripts/validate-pr-body.ts

Done-means resolved in the validator's own tree:
  /Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development/open-brain/scripts/done-means/705-pre-push-base-selection.sh
```

The named check exists in **neither** the review tree nor on the review branch.
It passed on the strength of the primary checkout alone.

NEGATIVE CONTROL — a name present in no tree is still correctly refused, which
proves the pass above comes from the fallback and not from a slack matcher:

```
- Done-means: scripts/done-means/definitely-not-a-real-check-xyz.sh
=> Verification field 'Done-means' must name an existing repo-relative path;
   not found: ... (looked in: <faketree>, /Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development/open-brain)
```

## Impact

A lane that deletes, renames, or never commits its done-means check passes the
PR-body gate as long as the primary checkout still carries a file of that path.
The primary checkout sits on the integration branch and accumulates every check
ever merged, so the fallback is *most* likely to fire exactly when a lane's own
check is missing. The gate reports `Done-means resolved`, and the reader has no
reason to doubt it.

Mitigating (why this is DEFECT, not CRITICAL): the branch tier (#706/#714) and
`verify-lane` both resolve against the PR head, and verify-lane refuses a check
absent from a fresh checkout at the head. This gate is the early one, so the
failure is a false GREEN at PR-create time, not necessarily at merge.

## Done-means suggestion

`scripts/done-means/NNN-validator-rejects-foreign-tree.sh`:

1. RED-first: review tree WITHOUT the check, name a path that exists ONLY in the
   validator's own tree → the validator must REFUSE. (Passes today = the defect.)
2. Positive control: the same path present in the REVIEW tree → resolves, and
   the note names the tree under review.
3. Branch tier unbroken: absent on disk in both, present in `PR_HEAD_REF` →
   still resolves via `git cat-file -e` (do not regress #706/#714).
4. Assert on the ANNOUNCEMENT text (round 28: announcements rot unasserted) —
   the note must name WHICH tree answered.

Likely direction: drop `OWN_TREE` from the search set, or keep it only when
`reviewRoot === OWN_TREE` (the ordinary same-directory case), so it can never
answer FOR a different tree.

## Discussion (1)

### rodaddy — 2026-08-10T14:38:52Z

**DIRECTION.** The own-tree fallback is no longer a peer of the tree under review — it is a last resort that may only speak when nothing authoritative exists.

`requireDoneMeans` now asks the **tree under review**, then the **head ref**. When a head ref is known those two are AUTHORITATIVE TOGETHER: their combined "no" is the answer, `OWN_TREE` is not consulted at all, and the refusal states that in as many words — "The validator's own tree was NOT consulted: a head ref is known, so the branch answer is authoritative." The own tree may answer only when there is **no head ref whatsoever** (a human running the validator by hand, #706 clause d), and that note now carries its own weaker basis — "no head ref was available ... this does NOT prove the path is present in the change under review" — instead of reading identically to a branch-backed pass.

**WHY THIS SHAPE, AND NOT THE ONE THE ISSUE SUGGESTED.** The issue proposed dropping `OWN_TREE`, or keeping it only when `reviewRoot === OWN_TREE`. Both were driven and rejected against the existing suite: `706-done-means-resolves-pr-head.sh` clause (d) runs the validator from a NEUTRAL cwd with no review root, so `reviewRoot !== OWN_TREE` in the very case that must keep passing, and the same-directory restriction breaks it. The load-bearing distinction is not *which directory* the review root happens to be — it is **whether an authoritative answer exists to be overruled**. Keying on the head ref expresses that; keying on directory identity only approximates it.

**WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE.** `.claude/hooks/pr-body-gate.ts` runs the PRIMARY checkout's copy of the validator, and that checkout sits on the integration branch, accumulating every done-means check ever merged. So the fallback fired most readily in exactly the case it should have caught — a lane that deleted, renamed, or never committed its own check — and printed `Done-means resolved` while doing it. #706's own defect, surviving one layer deeper because that lane fixed which tree is asked FIRST and left the wrong tree in the list.

**RECEIPTS.**

- Done-means: `scripts/done-means/720-validator-rejects-foreign-tree.sh`, 7 clauses. **RED 4/7** before the fix existed (1, 2, 5, 6 failing), **GREEN 7/7** after.
- Clause 5 drives the **REAL** path — a PreToolUse payload through `.claude/hooks/pr-body-gate.ts` with a genuine `gh pr create --head <branch>` — and its RED run showed the hook itself ALLOWING a body whose cited check was absent from the branch (exit=0). This issue's reproduction stopped at the validator; the defect reached the gate's published verdict.
- The legitimate cases the tiers exist for are intact and were re-run on the branch: **706 5/5**, **709 5/5**, **714 6/6**, plus `pr-template-passes-validator` 3/3, `done-means-field-required` 5/5, `pr-body-gate-fires` 8/8, `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean, `bun test scripts` 371 pass / 0 fail.
- `verify-lane 723`: **VERIFIED**, check exit 0 from a fresh worktree at head `f758ece0`, SHA-bound receipt on the PR.
- PR #723, squash-merged to `wip/2026-08-07` as `38719c9`. CI green across check, contract-parity, db-integration, python-*, validate, GitGuardian.

**ONE SELF-CAUGHT DEFECT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE INTERESTING PART.** The first draft of the new refusal reworded the "where it looked" text and turned `709-hook-feeds-head-ref.sh` clause 4 RED — that clause pins the literal `looked in:` string precisely because a refusal that stops saying where it looked is a dead end (round 29). The reflex is to update the sibling check to match the new code; doing so would have quietly deleted a round-29 tightening. Repaired in the direction of the check instead — the new message keeps the marker verbatim — and per round 28 the whole corrected clause set was then re-proved RED against the pre-fix validator before any green was claimed.

**STATE.** MERGED to `wip/2026-08-07`; not deployed anywhere, as this is repo-local PR gating with no runtime surface. RUNNING and observed this session: PR #723's own body was gated by the fixed validator through the live hook, announcing "resolved in the tree under review".

Lessons were RETURNED for the tracking-scribe rather than written into `docs/lane-contract.md` by this lane (four parallel gate lanes, one scribe owning root graph writes); they are in the `harvested:` comment on #723. The headline: **a fallback tree is still a tree, and Family A survives in fallbacks long after the primary lookup is repaired.**
